pr_body:
Rework of #79936.
Fixes #79798.

Adds the new flag `frame_incomplete` to `struct display_buffer_descriptor` that indicates that more writes will follow in the current frame.

This allows GUIs to communicate where, at multi-write frames, the frame ends.
This in turn allows display to understand the frame border, which can be useful for page flipping or "tearing enable" signal handling.

For more discussion, see #79936.

The effect of this change is that displays can now present multi-writes at once, to prevent the 'rolling shutter' effect of multiple separate partial writes, like so:

Before:
![without_view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3addb3c-7f14-42fc-b934-f8a09a23371b)

After:
![with_view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d40fed4-f619-4d58-afa0-ee2ba9b06616)

issue_context.title: display: Support page flipping
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
We have a display that supports writing to it and then page flipping to update all pixels on the screen at once.

Sadly, Zephyr's display API only supports this partially:
- `SCREEN_INFO_DOUBLE_BUFFER` already exists (for probably this very reason)
- No `pageflip` api function exists yet

Further, LVGL supports this (`lv_disp_flush_is_last`), but it does not get used by Zephyr yet.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
- Implement a `display_pageflip` Display Subsystem API function
- Use `lv_disp_flush_is_last` and call the `display_pageflip` function to pass this information on to the display

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Instead of adding a `display_pageflip`, this could be an extra flag in the `display_write` function. Although this would be a breaking change.
